rawFindings.title: v1 object decoder now serializes synthetic back-reference fields
rawFindings.explanation: For a v1 object containing a self-reference field such as `this$0`, the decoder now stores that field on the output object instead of skipping it. That means `decode(...).` on inputs like the `ConnectionRequest` payload will now include an extra `this$0` property pointing back to the object, whereas the previous behavior omitted the synthetic Java back-reference from the public result.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the guard that skips `this$<n>` fields when building the decoded object, while still advancing the stream position by decoding their values.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Decoding a v1 `ConnectionRequest` buffer now returns `{ ctx: { id: 101, this$0: [Circular] } }` instead of `{ ctx: { id: 101 } }`, so `JSON.stringify`/equality checks against the expected public shape fail.

rawFindings.title: v2 object decoder now exposes synthetic back-reference fields
rawFindings.explanation: For Hessian 2.0 objects, fields named like `this$0` are Java compiler-generated back-references and were previously omitted from the decoded result. The new assignment now includes them, which changes the public decoded shape and introduces circular references into objects that callers previously could stringify and compare normally.
rawFindings.suggestion: Keep decoding the field value to preserve stream alignment, but skip assigning names matching `/^this\$\d+$/` into the returned object.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Decoding the `v2/object/ConnectionRequest` fixture now yields `connreq.ctx.this$0 === connreq`, so code that expects `connreq.ctx` to only contain `id` breaks and `JSON.stringify(connreq)` throws on the circular reference.
